strategy.bottleneck: [DRAM-bandwidth-bound] GroupNorm pipeline: gn_apply_kernel (125.7us, DRAM 85.6% of peak, long_scoreboard 94.1%) plus gn_stats_kernel (45.9us, DRAM 89.0%). strategy.primary_optimisation_method: Single-pass fusion of gn_stats + gn_apply into ONE persistent cooperative kernel with a grid-wide barrier: each block reduces its own contiguous chunk (phase 1), grid.sync(), then re-reads the *same addresses* it just touched (phase 2) so they hit L2 instead of DRAM, applying affine+SiLU(+residual) and storing. This removes one full 67MB DRAM read pass per GroupNorm (134MB per forward) and one kernel launch/tail, exactly matching the DRAM-bound, near-zero-compute profile.

7. `cg::this_grid().sync();`
8. Phase 2 head: thread 0 sums the 4 partials of its group in fixed index order (identical arithmetic order to today's stage-2 loop, so numerics are unchanged), computes mean=sum*inv_n, rstd=rsqrtf(max(sq*inv_n-mean*mean,0)+eps) into smem; threads <cpg load gamma/beta and precompute a=gamma*rstd, b=beta-mean*a into smem (keep existing FMA form so the inner loop is one FMA + one SiLU per element).

strategy.modification_plan:
CHECKLIST
1. In fused_resblock, replace the monolithic pipeline with a batch-chunk loop. Exact actions: compute per_sample_bytes = C*H*W*4; chunk = clamp((int)(12*1024*1024 / per_sample_bytes), 1, B); additionally raise chunk until (chunk*32*seg_est) >= 2*170 blocks so GN grids keep >=340 blocks (for B=8,C=256,64x128: per_sample=8MB -> chunk=2, 4 iterations). Allocate ONCE before the loop: at::Tensor ybuf = at::empty({chunk,C,H,W}, xc.options()); at::Tensor zbuf = at::empty_like(ybuf); at::Tensor out = at::empty_like(xc). Reusing the same allocations keeps identical physical addresses hot in L2 across chunks.
2. Loop body (exact): for (int64_t b0=0;b0<B;b0+=chunk){ int64_t nb=std::min(chunk,B-b0); at::Tensor xs = xc.narrow(0,b0,nb); at::Tensor y = (nb==chunk? ybuf : ybuf.narrow(0,0,nb)); at::conv2d_out-style: y.copy_ is NOT used; instead call at::Tensor yv = at::conv2d(xs,w1c,{},ones,pads,ones,1); (keep cuDNN mainloop) then gn_silu_launch(yv,g1,b1,nullptr,yv,eps); at::Tensor zv = at::conv2d(yv,w2c,{},ones,pads,ones,1); at::Tensor os = out.narrow(0,b0,nb); gn_silu_launch(zv,g2,b2,xs.data_ptr<float>(),os,eps); }  Ensure xs/os are contiguous slices (narrow on dim0 of a contiguous tensor is contiguous) so all existing pointer arithmetic in the GN kernels stays valid.
3. Fix stream: replace at::cuda::getDefaultCUDAStream() with at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream() in gn_silu_launch so chunks serialize on the benchmarked stream.
4. Keep the per-chunk `part` buffer allocation out of the loop as well: allocate part once with size max_groups*seg*2 (max_groups = chunk*32) and pass it in, avoiding caching-allocator churn per chunk.
5. GN launch config per chunk: ngroups = nb*32; keep seg = clamp((n+2047)/2048,1,32) and by = clamp(n/(256*8),1,256); verify grid_s.x*grid_s.y and grid_a.x*grid_a.y each >= 340 blocks; if not, increase chunk (step 1 guard).
6. Optional (gated, only if step 1-5 measured win is <5%): set an L2 accessPolicyWindow via cudaStreamSetAttribute on ybuf/zbuf pointers with hitRatio 1.0 and cudaAccessPropertyPersisting, resetting after the loop.
7. Correctness: GN statistics are per (sample,group); chunking over the batch dimension is mathematically identical (no cross-sample reduction). Conv is per-sample independent. Reduction order within a group is unchanged (same seg partition when nb==chunk). Residual add reads xs, never mutated.

strategy.modification_plan:
1. In fused_resblock, right after the contiguity hygiene, create half copies used ONLY as conv operands/intermediates: `auto xh = xc.to(at::kHalf); auto w1h = w1c.to(at::kHalf); auto w2h = w2c.to(at::kHalf);`. Keep the original fp32 `xc` untouched for the residual add. Do NOT touch norm weights/bias (stay fp32).
2. Replace `at::Tensor y = at::conv2d(xc,w1c,...)` with `at::Tensor y = at::conv2d(xh, w1h, {}, {1,1},{1,1},{1,1},1);` (half in -> half out, cuDNN uses fp32 accumulate). Same for conv2: `at::Tensor z = at::conv2d(y, w2h, ...)`. Both intermediates are now 33.5MB instead of 67MB.
3. Retemplate gn_stats_kernel on element type: for half input use `const uint4*` (8 halves = 16B, fully coalesced, replaces the float4 path). Per group n = cpg*H*W/8 = 65536/8 = 8192. Inside the loop: `uint4 v = xp[i]; const __half2* h = reinterpret_cast<const __half2*>(&v);` then `#pragma unroll for(j=0..3){ float2 f = __half22float2(h[j]); sum += f.x+f.y; sq = fmaf(f.x,f.x, fmaf(f.y,f.y, sq)); }`. All accumulation stays fp32; keep the identical fixed-segment (seg) two-stage deterministic reduction and no atomics.
4. Retemplate gn_apply_kernel as `<typename OutT, bool RES>` with half input read as uint4 (8 elements/iteration). Channel index: hwv = HW/8 = 1024, so shift = 10 and `ch = i>>10` still holds (no divide). Compute `t = fmaf(f, sc[ch], sb[ch]); o = t/(1.f+expf(-t));` in fp32 for all 8 lanes.
5. First GN call (after conv1): OutT = __half, RES=false, writes the 8 results back as one uint4 via `__floats2half2_rn` pairs -> in-place into y (our own buffer). Second GN call (after conv2): OutT = float, RES=true; read residual as two float4 loads from `xc` (8 floats), add, and store two float4s into the fp32 output. Output allocation stays `at::empty_like(xc)` (fp32, same device).
6. Keep inv_n = 1/(cpg*HW) = 1/65536 (element count unchanged); keep eps/rstd math in fp32; keep the shared sc/sb per-channel affine precompute (a = gamma*rstd, b = beta - mean*a) so the inner loop is pure FMA.
7. Adjust gn_silu_launch: vector width constant 8 for half (require HW%8==0, true for 64x128), 4 for the fp32 residual/out path; assert 16B alignment of all half pointers (ATen allocations are 256B aligned).
8. Guard: if `x.scalar_type()!=kFloat` or HW%8!=0, fall back to the existing fp32 float4 path (keep the old template instantiations compiled).
9. Validate max_atol on the fixed workload; if it exceeds 2.8e-3, restrict fp16 to conv2 only (conv1 stays fp32) as the fallback knob.
